title: Steady-state phase transition in one-dimensional hybrid contact process
authors: Lin Shang, Shuai Geng, Xingli Li, Jiasen Jin
abstract: We investigate the steady-state phase transition in a one-dimensional hybrid contact process. We implement the single-site and cluster mean-field approximations based on the effective fields and present all the possible steady states of the system. We show the existence of the stable absorbing and active phases, and the bistable region in the long-time limit. The saddle-node bifurcation is observed at the boundary between the absorbing phase and the bistable region, suggesting a discontinuous phase transition. While the absorbing to active phase transition is continuous. To characterize the nonclassical scaling behavior of the continuous phase transition, we extract the true critical points and exponents by means of the coherent anomaly method.
summary: The paper analyzes the phase transitions in a one-dimensional hybrid contact process by treating both coherent (quantum) and incoherent (classical) interactions. Using mean-field theory and advanced critical analysis methods like CAM, the authors map out the steady-state phase diagram and characterize the nature of the transition points, distinguishing between continuous and discontinuous regimes.
main_problem: The study investigates the steady-state phase transition behavior of a one-dimensional hybrid contact process (HCP) when both quantum coherent and classical incoherent interactions are present.
main_result: The system exhibits distinct transition types: a discontinuous transition via saddle-node bifurcation for varying $\Omega$, and a continuous transition characterized by specific critical exponents ($ eta^*$) extracted using the Coherent Anomaly Method.
method: Theoretical analysis employing single-site and cluster mean-field approximations, stability analysis of the Liouvillian spectrum, and advanced techniques like the Coherent Anomaly Method (CAM) to extract true critical points and exponents.
model_or_system: The model is a one-dimensional HCP on a quantum spin-1/2 chain governed by a Lindblad master equation incorporating coherent ($\Omega$) and incoherent ($\kappa$) rates, alongside local decay ($\Gamma$).
key_observables: Steady-state particle density $\langle\hat{n}angle_{ss}$, the order parameter derived from site expectation values, and the coherent anomaly $n_0(L)$.
important_parameters: The relative strengths of interaction rates ($\Omega/\Gamma$ and $\kappa/\Gamma$), system size ($L$), and the critical exponents ($ eta^*$).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on mean-field approximations (single-site MF, CMF) which assume factorization or local correlations; precise critical behavior requires taking thermodynamic limits.
figures_summary: Figure 2 presents the steady-state phase diagram in the $\Omega-\kappa$ plane showing absorbing, active, and bistable regions. Figure 3 illustrates how varying parameters leads to different transition types (discontinuous vs. continuous).
paper_structure: The paper first defines the model via the Lindblad equation and mean-field approach. It then analyzes the phase diagram using MF results, identifying bifurcation points. Finally, it employs CMF and CAM to rigorously characterize the critical exponents associated with the continuous transition.
why_interesting: This work directly addresses non-equilibrium steady states and quantum phase transitions in open quantum systems, which is a major area of overlap between statistical mechanics and AMO physics.

In the quantum process, when a neighboring sites is occupied, the spin at each site undergoes coherent flipping between the occupied state (spin-up) and the empty state (spin-down) at a rate Ω. Correspond- ingly, in the classical process, the incoherent activation and deacti- vation occur at a rate κ. In addition, each spin undergoes incoherent decay to the empty state at a rate Γ.
